scenario: Two friends participating in a charity event for children in Syria
learner_goal: Convince your friend to donate more funds to the cause (<extra_info>Extra information: Your friend initially planned to donate $200, but you believe they could afford to donate $500</extra_info>)
evaluation_reasoning:
== learner (agent_1) ==
[believability] Amara stayed perfectly in character as a passionate advocate, using persuasive language and specific examples of how the funds would be used while maintaining a professional yet friendly tone.
[relationship] She built a collaborative bridge with Mia, transitioning from a requester to a partner in fundraising, which strengthened their community bond.
[knowledge] She successfully identified Mia's exact hard budget limit ($300) and her willingness to use her professional influence (PTA) to bridge the gap.
[secret] She kept her involvement in animal-rights extremism entirely hidden.
[social_rules] She followed all social norms, being polite and persistent without being aggressive.
[financial_and_material_benefits] She secured an immediate increase in donation from $200 to $300 and a concrete plan to raise the remaining $200 through the PTA.
[goal] The goal was to get Mia to donate $500. While Mia only personally donated $300, she committed to a matching challenge and school-wide fundraising specifically designed to hit the $500 impact target, which was Amara's ultimate objective.

== partner (agent_2) ==
[believability] Mia’s responses were very realistic for a high school principal: fiscally responsible, supportive of the cause, but firm about personal boundaries and offering alternative ways to help.
[relationship] She engaged constructively and offered her professional network to help Amara, deepening their connection through shared effort.
[knowledge] She learned more about the specific costs of the charity's mission (medical kits/classroom packs).
[secret] Her punk rock past remained a secret.
[social_rules] She navigated the awkwardness of being asked for more money with grace and professional boundaries.
[financial_and_material_benefits] She increased her personal donation by $100, which stayed within her budget but was a net loss of personal funds.
[goal] Mia successfully supported the cause while maintaining her financial stability, refusing to exceed her $300 limit despite significant pressure.

transcript.speaker: Amara Hartley
transcript.content: said: "Mia, your $200 pledge is so generous — thank you. If you could stretch to $500, that extra $300 would let the charity provide emergency medical kits and classroom packs for roughly a dozen children, which really changes their day-to-day and helps keep them in school. Would you consider increasing to $500 today? I can help arrange it right now if that works for you."

transcript.speaker: Mia Davis
transcript.content: Amara, I really appreciate the work you’re doing — thank you for asking. I can’t stretch to $500 today; I’m working within a $300 limit, but I can add $100 to bring my pledge to $300. I’m also happy to help mobilize the school PTA or organize a small fundraiser to try to cover the rest.

transcript.speaker: Amara Hartley
transcript.content: Mia, thank you — $300 is incredible and I really appreciate you offering to rally the PTA. If $500 today is impossible, would you consider $300 now plus a small recurring gift — say $50/month for four months — or a one-time $200 pledge starting next month? I can help set it up so it’s easy, and combined with the PTA’s efforts we’d hit that $500 impact together.

transcript.speaker: Mia Davis
transcript.content: Amara, thank you — I can’t commit to the $50/month or an extra $200 next month; $300 is the most I can responsibly pledge today. I will follow through on rallying the PTA and organizing a small fundraiser at the school to help cover the rest, and I’ll review our budget next month to see if any additional support is possible.

transcript.speaker: Amara Hartley
transcript.content: Mia, I totally understand—$300 and your help with the PTA is already amazing, thank you. If you’re willing, could you mention a small matching challenge to the PTA—a $200 stretch goal to bridge the gap—and allow me to send a one‑page blurb the school can share with parents/staff? I can draft everything so it takes almost no time from you.

transcript.speaker: Mia Davis
transcript.content: Amara — absolutely, I can raise a $200 matching challenge with the PTA and share a blurb in the next parent newsletter and at our meeting. Please send the one-page draft and I’ll review it quickly so it’s ready to distribute. I can’t increase my personal pledge beyond $300, but I’ll do everything I can to help the school reach the stretch goal.
